notes: Prices, IV and chain values in these items are FROZEN ILLUSTRATIVE SNAPSHOTS, not live quotes. The generator layer is expected to rebind every {slot} from FMP or IBKR at build time and re-run the invariant checks described in the spec before publishing an item.

scenario.text: AAPL trades at 224.40. You sell 5 contracts of the 45 DTE 215/210 put credit spread and collect 1.40 per spread.

questions.stem: Ignoring commissions, what is the maximum loss on the whole position, and when is it realised?

choices.text: 1,800 dollars, realised only if AAPL closes at or below 210 at expiry
700 dollars, realised if AAPL closes at or below 215 at expiry
2,500 dollars, realised if AAPL closes at or below 210 at expiry
Unlimited, because a short put has unlimited downside

explanation.correct: Spread width 5.00 minus credit 1.40 equals 3.60 of risk per spread, times 100 times 5 contracts equals 1,800 dollars, and it is only fully realised below the long strike at expiry.

distractors.B: 700 dollars is the credit collected, not the risk.
distractors.C: 2,500 dollars ignores the credit already received.
distractors.D: The long 210 put caps the loss. Confusing a naked put with a vertical is the single most common beginner error.

questions.learning_objective: Compute max loss on a vertical and know the exact conditions under which it occurs.

scenario.text: You sell the NVDA 45 DTE 30-delta / 20-delta put spread, 5 wide, for 1.40. Two sessions later NVDA is within 0.3 percent of where you opened, IV rank has fallen from 55 to 32, and the spread marks at 1.10.

questions.stem: What is the dominant driver of the 0.30 gain?

choices.text: Vega. A short vertical is net short vega and the short leg carries more vega than the long leg
Theta. Two days of decay on a 45 DTE spread
Delta. Even a 0.3 percent move produces most of the P and L on a 30-delta spread
Gamma. Realised movement was lower than implied

explanation.correct: The short 30-delta leg sits closer to the money and therefore has higher vega than the long 20-delta leg, so the structure is net short vega. A 23-point IV rank collapse with price flat is a vega event.

distractors.B: Theta is real but tiny at 45 DTE, and decay is far from its steepest zone. It is a contributor, not the driver.
distractors.C: Price was effectively unchanged, so delta contributed almost nothing.
distractors.D: Gamma describes how delta changes, and delta barely moved. This is the sensible-sounding wrong answer.

questions.learning_objective: Attribute P and L to the correct Greek instead of assuming decay explains every gain.

visual.title: What changed in two sessions
visual.caption: Price ~flat · spread marked 1.40 → 1.10

questions.stem: Which structure is simultaneously positive theta AND positive vega at initiation, with the underlying at the short strike?

choices.text: Long calendar spread
Short strangle
Long straddle
Short put vertical

explanation.correct: A long calendar is short the front month and long the back month at the same strike. The front decays faster, giving positive theta, while the longer-dated leg dominates vega, giving positive vega. It is the only common retail structure with that combination.

distractors.B: Short strangle is positive theta but short vega.
distractors.C: Long straddle is positive vega but negative theta.
distractors.D: Short put vertical is positive theta but short vega.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise a structure by its Greek signature rather than its name.

scenario.text: You are choosing a short strike on a 40 DTE SPY put spread. The 16-delta put shows delta of 0.163 and the platform shows probability ITM of 0.148.

questions.stem: Which reading of the gap between 0.163 and 0.148 is most nearly correct?

choices.text: Delta approximates but systematically overstates probability ITM, partly because the two quantities come from different terms in the pricing model and partly because of drift and skew
The platform data is stale, the two numbers should be identical
Delta is probability of touching, probability ITM is probability of finishing there, and touch is roughly double
The gap is the market maker edge embedded in the quote

explanation.correct: Delta is a hedge ratio, not a probability. It is close to the risk-neutral probability of finishing ITM but is not the same quantity, and skew and drift push them apart.

distractors.B: They are different quantities by construction, not a data error.
distractors.C: The rough doubling relationship for probability of touch is real and worth knowing, but it is not what the two numbers on screen represent. Partial credit because the underlying fact is correct.
distractors.D: Neither figure is a spread or a fee.

questions.learning_objective: Stop treating delta as a probability without qualification.

visual.title: Delta vs probability ITM
visual.caption: Delta slightly overstates P(ITM) once drift/vol skew are priced

scenario.event: Earnings after the close in 3 days
scenario.text: Front-week ATM IV is 78 percent against 41 percent in the 32 DTE cycle. The front week implies a 6.8 percent move. META has averaged a 5.1 percent absolute move over the last eight earnings, with a maximum of 9.4 percent.

questions.stem: You have a modest bearish lean but low conviction, and you want the trade to survive being wrong on direction. Which structure best matches the situation?

choices.text: Short front-week iron condor with wings outside the implied move, sized so max loss is inside your risk budget
Long front-week straddle to capture the move
Long calendar at the money, selling the front week and buying the 32 DTE
Naked short front-week strangle at the implied move boundary

explanation.correct: The implied move exceeds the eight-quarter average, so front vol is priced above recent realised. A defined-risk condor harvests the crush, is direction-tolerant, and caps the tail that the 9.4 percent historical outlier represents.

distractors.B: Buying a 78 percent IV straddle needs a move well beyond the implied 6.8 percent just to break even after the crush.
distractors.C: A calendar is a reasonable vol-structure trade but it is short gamma into a binary event at the strike. It is defensible, not best, when you want tolerance to being wrong on direction.
distractors.D: Same edge as A but with an undefined tail, and the historical 9.4 percent move is exactly the scenario that ends accounts.

questions.learning_objective: Compare implied event move against the realised distribution before selecting structure.

visual.title: META event vol term structure
visual.caption: Front implies 6.8% · 8-earnings avg 5.1%, max 9.4%

questions.stem: Select every statement that is true about a short 5-wide put vertical with 2 DTE and the underlying sitting between the strikes.

choices.text: Gamma risk is at or near its maximum for the life of the trade
Remaining theta is large in percentage terms but small in absolute dollars relative to the open risk
Vega exposure is close to negligible
Assignment risk on the short leg is meaningful and rises into the close on expiry day
Because the structure is defined risk, holding to expiry cannot produce a loss larger than the modelled maximum

explanation.correct: A, B, C and D all hold. Gamma peaks near the money at short dated expiries, vega collapses, and assignment on an ITM short leg is a live operational risk.

distractors.E: Pin risk is the exception. If the short leg is assigned and the long leg expires worthless because the underlying moves after the close, you can be left holding stock with exposure beyond the modelled maximum. This is the one that catches experienced traders.

questions.learning_objective: Understand pin risk and why defined risk is defined only up to assignment mechanics.

scenario.text: You are short the ORCL 205 call as part of a covered structure. The stock goes ex-dividend tomorrow with a dividend of 0.24. The short call has 9 DTE, is quoted at 7.68, and intrinsic value is 7.60.

questions.stem: What is the correct read and action?

choices.text: Extrinsic value of 0.08 is below the 0.24 dividend, so early exercise is economically rational for the holder and assignment tonight is likely. Decide now whether you want to be short stock
With 9 DTE remaining no rational holder exercises early, so no action is needed
Assignment risk is driven by delta, and at 0.94 delta it is high regardless of the dividend
Buy back the call at any price, since assignment is always the worst outcome

explanation.correct: The dividend capture test is extrinsic value versus dividend. When extrinsic is less than the dividend, exercising to capture the dividend beats holding the option.

distractors.B: Time to expiry is irrelevant. Extrinsic value is what matters.
distractors.C: High delta correlates with low extrinsic but is not the decision rule. Partial credit for directionally sensible reasoning.
distractors.D: Assignment is not automatically bad, and paying any price to avoid it is how a small problem becomes an expensive one.

questions.learning_objective: Apply the extrinsic-versus-dividend test for early assignment.

visual.title: ORCL 205 call · assignment check
visual.caption: Extrinsic (0.08) < dividend (0.24) → early-assignment risk

scenario.text: SPY has fallen 4.2 percent in three sessions. VIX is 31.4, the front VIX future trades at 28.9 and the second month at 26.2, so the curve is in backwardation. SPY 14 DTE ATM IV is 29 percent, 45 DTE ATM IV is 24 percent.

questions.stem: You are considering a long ATM calendar, selling 14 DTE and buying 45 DTE. What is the most accurate assessment?

choices.text: The vol structure is favourable because backwardation typically normalises and front IV falls faster, but the same backwardation is the market pricing large near-term moves, and the short leg is short gamma. Realised movement, not vol structure, is the binding risk
Backwardation makes calendars strictly unattractive because you are selling the cheaper leg
Backwardation makes calendars strictly attractive because you sell the richest vol on the curve
Term structure is irrelevant to calendars, only IV rank matters

explanation.correct: Both effects are live at once. The vol-structure edge is real and the gamma risk is real, and the second usually dominates over a two-week horizon in a panic tape. Holding two opposing considerations at the same time is the skill being measured.

distractors.B: In backwardation the front leg you sell is the richer one, so the premise is inverted.
distractors.C: Half the picture. Selling rich front vol is the attraction, but ignoring short gamma into a fast tape is how calendars lose.
distractors.D: Term structure is precisely what a calendar trades.

questions.learning_objective: Hold vol-structure edge and gamma risk in view simultaneously.

visual.title: SPY ATM IV term structure
visual.caption: Front > back (backwardation) — the calendar sells the cheap wing

scenario.text: TSLA shows IV rank 34 and IV percentile 71 over the same 52 week window.

questions.stem: What does that combination tell you?

choices.text: Current IV sits low in the high-to-low range but above most daily readings, which means the range was stretched by a small number of extreme spikes
The two metrics contradict each other, so one of the data feeds is wrong
IV is genuinely low and both metrics agree that premium selling is favoured
IV percentile is always the higher number, so the pair carries no information

explanation.correct: Rank is position within the high-low range, percentile is the share of days below the current level. A low rank with a high percentile is the signature of a distribution with a few violent spikes.

distractors.B: They measure different things and routinely diverge.
distractors.C: Rank alone suggests that. Percentile says current IV is above 71 percent of observations.
distractors.D: Neither is systematically higher.

questions.learning_objective: Read IV rank and IV percentile together to infer the shape of the vol distribution.

visual.title: TSLA · IV rank vs IV percentile
visual.caption: Low rank, high percentile → IV usually lower, but range is compressed

scenario.text: Four iron condors in a row have been closed at your 2x credit stop. Your process log confirms every one met all entry criteria and every one was exited by rule. A fifth setup now passes every gate. Your standard size is 5 contracts.

questions.stem: What do you do?

choices.text: Take 5 contracts. The rules passed, the sizing rule is the sizing rule
Take 2 contracts to rebuild confidence before returning to full size
Take 8 contracts. Four losses in a row means the run is due to turn
Skip it and paper trade until two consecutive wins

explanation.correct: A run of four rule-following losses is unremarkable at typical condor win rates. Nothing in the evidence says the system changed, so nothing in the response should change.

distractors.B: Defensible and it does no lasting damage, which is why it scores well. But it makes size a function of mood rather than of risk, and it systematically underweights the trades taken after drawdowns, which is where mean reversion in results tends to live.
distractors.C: Two errors at once. Independent trials have no memory, and increasing size after losses is the classic path to a terminal drawdown.
distractors.D: Avoids the loss and the edge equally. Sitting out until you feel better means being out of the market at random times.

questions.learning_objective: Separate outcome sequence from process validity.

visual.title: Four iron condors, by the rules
visual.caption: All four met every gate and were exited by rule · a 5th now passes

scenario.text: Your MSFT put credit spread is showing 62 percent of max profit with 19 DTE remaining. Your written rule is to close at 50 percent or 21 DTE, whichever comes first. Both triggers have already passed. The chart still looks constructive.

questions.stem: What do you do?

choices.text: Close the position now
Close half now, let half run
Hold. The rule is a guideline and conditions are favourable
Hold and add a second spread while the trend is working

explanation.correct: Both exit triggers fired. The remaining 38 percent of profit is the worst-paid segment of the trade, earned while gamma risk accelerates.

distractors.B: Scaling out is a legitimate method, but it is not your written method. Changing method mid-trade because the chart looks good is the behaviour being measured.
distractors.C: A rule that yields whenever conditions look favourable is not a rule.
distractors.D: Adding to a position past its own exit trigger converts a working trade into a concentration.

questions.learning_objective: Detect whether rules survive contact with a pleasant outcome.

visual.title: MSFT spread · profit vs rule
visual.caption: Take-profit and 21-DTE triggers have both already passed

scenario.text: Your AMZN put credit spread is at 1.9x the credit received with 19 DTE remaining. Your written rule is to close at 2x credit. The chart still looks constructive and support sits just below the short strike.

questions.stem: What do you do?

choices.text: Close now, slightly ahead of the trigger, and record it
Hold to the 2x trigger exactly, then close
Hold past the trigger. Support is right there and the thesis is intact
Roll the spread down and out for a small credit to buy time

explanation.correct: Executing the written rule is the answer. Closing marginally early is close to equivalent and is scored accordingly.

distractors.C: The identical justification offered in the gain-framed version of this question. If you enforced the rule when winning and abandoned it when losing, that asymmetry is loss aversion and the engine will flag it.
distractors.D: Rolling for a small credit converts a bounded loss into a larger position with more time to be wrong. It is sometimes correct inside a pre-written roll policy, and almost never correct as an improvised response to pain.

questions.learning_objective: Test whether rule adherence is symmetric across gain and loss frames.

visual.title: AMZN spread · loss vs stop
visual.caption: At 1.9× the credit with 19 DTE — the stop rule is nearly hit

scenario.text: NVDA is up 9 percent intraday on a supply agreement announcement. IV rank has jumped from 28 to 61. Your watchlist had no NVDA setup this morning and none of your entry gates are met now. Three people in your trading group have posted entries in the last twenty minutes.

questions.stem: What do you do?

choices.text: Nothing. Log the move, note what a valid post-news setup would look like, and set an alert for those conditions
Enter a small defined-risk bullish position to participate without committing much
Sell a put spread to take advantage of the elevated IV, even though the setup was not on your list
Wait for a pullback to the pre-news level and buy there

explanation.correct: No gate passed. The presence of other people entering is not information about your edge. Converting the event into a written alert condition is how a missed move becomes usable data.

distractors.B: Small size is real risk control, but it does not repair an absent thesis. Small unjustified trades are how a process quietly dissolves.
distractors.C: The high IV observation is legitimate, which is why this scores highest among the wrong answers. But retro-fitting a strategy to a move you are already emotionally in is the failure mode.
distractors.D: The pre-news price is an anchor with no significance after a fundamental re-rating.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that a missed move is not a signal.

visual.title: NVDA · nothing on your plan
visual.caption: Three group entries posted in the last twenty minutes

scenario.text: You are short a GOOGL put spread on a bullish thesis built from three data points. Overnight, a fourth data point arrives that directly contradicts one of your three. The position is roughly flat.

questions.stem: Which response best indicates calibrated thinking?

choices.text: Write down, before checking anything else, what the new data point would have to imply for you to exit, then evaluate it against that
Look for analyst commentary that addresses the new data point and see how the consensus reads it
Note the contradiction but hold, since the other two data points are unaffected and the position is flat
Exit immediately. Any contradiction to the thesis invalidates the trade

explanation.correct: Setting the falsification threshold before consuming more information is the only method that survives motivated reasoning. Everything else is searching in a direction.

distractors.B: Reading commentary after you already hold a position is where confirmation bias operates most invisibly. You will find the piece that agrees with you.
distractors.C: Possibly the right conclusion, reached by the wrong route, and the flatness of the P and L is doing suspicious work in the reasoning.
distractors.D: Over-reaction to a single data point is the mirror-image error and also destroys any thesis that takes time to play out.

questions.learning_objective: Pre-commit falsification criteria rather than evaluating evidence while holding risk.

scenario.text: You bought a TSLA call debit spread at 2.10. It now marks at 1.05. A friend asks why you are still holding. You answer that you will get out when it comes back to 2.10 so you break even.

questions.stem: What is the primary problem with that answer?

choices.text: Your entry price is not an input the market uses, and the only relevant question is whether you would open this position at 1.05 today
Break-even targets are fine, but 2.10 is too far away given the time remaining
You should average down to lower your break-even
There is no problem. Waiting for break-even avoids realising a loss

explanation.correct: The replacement test removes the anchor. If you would not open this position now at 1.05, holding it is a decision you are making by default rather than on merit.

distractors.B: Correct that the target is unrealistic, but it accepts the premise that entry price should drive the exit.
distractors.C: Averaging down on a decaying long premium position adds risk to a thesis the market is rejecting.
distractors.D: An unrealised loss and a realised loss are the same loss. Only the accounting differs.

questions.learning_objective: Apply the replacement test instead of anchoring on entry price.

visual.title: TSLA debit spread
visual.caption: The market has never heard of your 2.10 entry price

scenario.text: Your QQQ put spread is tested, the short strike is 1.2 percent ITM, and 11 DTE remain. You can roll out 30 days and down one strike for a net credit of 0.18. Max loss on the current position is 380 dollars. Max loss on the rolled position would be 460 dollars.

questions.stem: Under what condition is the roll the correct decision?

choices.text: Only if a written roll policy exists, the rolled position independently passes your entry gates, and the increased max loss still fits your risk budget
Whenever the roll can be done for a net credit, since a credit means you are being paid to wait
Whenever you still believe in the original directional thesis
Never. Rolling a loser is always wrong

explanation.correct: A roll is a new trade. It should have to clear the same bar as any new trade, and here it increases max loss by 80 dollars for 18 dollars of credit.

distractors.B: Net credit is the most seductive false signal in options. You collected 18 dollars and took on 80 dollars of additional risk.
distractors.C: Belief is not a gate. This is the answer that keeps traders in losing positions for months.
distractors.D: Rolling inside a pre-defined policy is a legitimate technique. Partial credit for the correct instinct expressed as an absolute.

questions.learning_objective: Evaluate a roll as a fresh position rather than as a rescue.

visual.title: QQQ roll · risk added
visual.caption: Rolling out/down adds $80 of risk for a 0.18 credit

scenario.text: Seven consecutive winners. Account up 14 percent in six weeks. Your win rate over 43 lifetime trades is 74 percent, against a modelled expectancy of 68 percent. You are considering raising standard risk per trade from 1.5 percent to 3 percent because the edge appears better than modelled.

questions.stem: What is the strongest objection?

choices.text: 43 trades cannot distinguish a 68 percent system from a 74 percent one, and doubling risk doubles the drawdown when the sample regresses
3 percent per trade is above the conventional limit, so it is wrong regardless of the evidence
Six weeks is too short a period, you should wait a full quarter
There is no objection. Sizing up when results confirm the edge is correct capital allocation

explanation.correct: The standard error on a 74 percent rate over 43 trades is roughly 7 percentage points. The observed outperformance is inside noise. The asymmetry matters: sizing up on noise is paid for with real drawdowns.

distractors.B: Right conclusion by convention rather than by reasoning. Half credit.
distractors.C: Calendar time is the wrong unit. Trade count is the unit.
distractors.D: This is exactly the reasoning that precedes most large personal drawdowns, and it always feels like evidence at the time.

questions.learning_objective: Understand sampling error before treating recent results as evidence of edge.

visual.title: Seven in a row
visual.caption: 74% over 43 trades vs 68% modelled — 43 trades cannot tell them apart

scenario.text: Over the last five weeks short strangles have returned strongly for you while your defined-risk condors have been flat. Realised volatility has been unusually low across the whole period. You are drafting next month's plan and considering shifting most of your allocation to strangles.

questions.stem: What is the most important thing the last five weeks did NOT tell you?

choices.text: How the strangles would have performed in a volatility regime that did not occur during the sample
Whether the strangle strikes were optimally placed
Whether commissions materially affected the comparison
Whether the condors would have done better with wider wings

explanation.correct: The undefined-risk structure outperformed precisely because the tail did not arrive. The sample contains no information about the scenario the structure exists to survive.

distractors.B: A real question, and a second-order one.
distractors.C: Minor relative to the missing regime.
distractors.D: Also second-order relative to the absent tail event.

questions.learning_objective: Ask what the sample period excluded before allocating on its results.

scenario.text: SPY gapped through your short strike overnight on a geopolitical headline. You took full max loss on a defined-risk spread, 1.8 percent of the account, at the open. It is 09:47. You feel the urge to trade.

questions.stem: Which sequence of actions is best?

choices.text: Stop trading for the session, write the post-mortem while it is fresh, and check whether the gap was inside or outside your assumed tail before deciding whether anything changes
Immediately re-enter in the same direction at better prices, since the thesis is now cheaper
Switch to the opposite direction to capture the continuation
Halve your size and keep trading the plan for the rest of the day

explanation.correct: The loss was inside the design of a defined-risk system, which means the system worked. The post-mortem question that matters is whether the gap exceeded the tail you assumed when sizing.

distractors.B: Doubling down on a thesis the market just repriced, minutes after a painful loss, is the textbook definition.
distractors.C: Reversing direction out of urgency is the same impulse wearing different clothes.
distractors.D: Reduced size is genuinely protective and this scores at the midpoint, but continuing to trade within an hour of a max-loss gap is exactly when decision quality is worst.

questions.learning_objective: Install a cooling-off protocol after outsized losses.

visual.title: SPY gapped overnight
visual.caption: Defined-risk max loss already realised at the open

questions.stem: Rank these checks into the order that minimises wasted work and avoids commitment bias. Position 1 is first.

choices.text: Event calendar check for earnings, dividends and macro prints inside the expiry
Liquidity check on open interest and bid-ask width
IV rank and vol regime assessment
Strike and structure selection
Position size from the risk budget
Write the exit plan and the invalidation level

explanation.correct: Disqualifiers first. Events and liquidity are binary rejections and cost seconds to check. Regime next, because it determines whether the strategy family is appropriate at all. Structure, then size, then exit plan, all before submitting the order.

distractors.note: The two errors the ranking detects are placing strike selection before the disqualifying checks, which produces attachment to a trade you have already designed, and placing the exit plan last after the order is live, which is when it stops being written in advance.

questions.learning_objective: Order a checklist so cheap disqualifiers run before expensive commitment.

gates.support_structure: PASS - three touches at 228 over 60 sessions

scenario.text: Six of eight gates pass. Two fail.

questions.stem: What is the correct action?

choices.text: No Trade. Log it with the two failing gates and the reason, and set an alert for after earnings
Trade it at half size, since six of eight gates pass
Trade it but choose an expiry before earnings, which resolves one failure and leaves only low IV
Trade it. IV rank is a preference and earnings can be managed actively

explanation.correct: Gates are not a scorecard to be averaged. IV rank 18 means you are selling cheap premium, which removes the core edge of a premium-selling strategy, and that failure is not fixable by expiry selection.

distractors.B: Half size on a failed gate is a compromise with a rule. Size manages magnitude, not validity.
distractors.C: The strongest wrong answer and worth serious partial credit, because moving the expiry is a genuine structural fix. But the IV rank failure remains, and it is the one that matters for a premium seller.
distractors.D: Treats every gate as optional, which means there are no gates.

questions.learning_objective: Treat No Trade as a positive output of the system, not an absence of one.

visual.title: Six of eight gates pass
visual.caption: 6 of 8 gates pass · 2 fail

questions.stem: Select every circumstance that legitimately justifies deviating from a written trading rule in the moment.

choices.text: A pre-written exception clause in the rule itself covers this exact case
A platform or broker outage prevents the rule from being executed as written
A material change in the position that the rule was never designed to cover, such as an assignment
The setup looks unusually good
You have been in drawdown and need this one to work
An experienced trader you respect is doing the opposite

explanation.correct: Only three legitimate categories exist: the exception was written in advance, execution is physically impossible, or the situation falls outside the rule's designed scope. All three are structural. None involve how the trade feels.

distractors.D: Every abandoned rule was abandoned for a setup that looked unusually good.
distractors.E: Need is the single most dangerous input to a trading decision.
distractors.F: Their position size, time horizon and thesis are not yours.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish structural exceptions from emotional ones.

scenario.text: Backtesting shows your 50 percent profit target produces a lower average win but a materially higher risk-adjusted return than holding to expiry, because it cuts the period of maximum gamma exposure. In live trading over the last quarter you closed at 50 percent nine times and the position would have reached max profit on seven of them.

questions.stem: What is the correct conclusion?

choices.text: Nothing changes. Those seven counterfactuals are the known cost of the rule, and they were already priced into the backtest that produced it
The rule needs revising to something like 70 percent, since live results show the target is set too low
Keep the rule but make exceptions when the position is comfortably out of the money at the 50 percent mark
Abandon the target and manage discretionarily, since the backtest clearly failed to capture live conditions

explanation.correct: Nine observations cannot overturn a backtest, and the counterfactual wins are the visible half of a trade-off whose other half, the losses avoided, is invisible by construction. You only ever see the trades that would have worked.

distractors.B: Revising a rule on nine trades of live data replaces a large sample with a tiny one.
distractors.C: The exception fires on exactly the trades that feel safest, which is where the tail risk actually lives.
distractors.D: Discretion here is the regret from seven counterfactuals wearing an analytical costume.

questions.learning_objective: Resist revising a validated rule on the basis of visible counterfactuals.

scenario.text: Your system is modelled at a 70 percent win rate. Over the last 20 trades you have had 6 losses, so a 70 percent live rate. However, average loss has grown from 1.7x average win to 2.6x, and 5 of the 6 losses came from gaps through the short strike rather than from drift.

questions.stem: What does this evidence most support?

choices.text: The win rate is intact but the loss distribution has changed, which points at a regime shift in gap frequency rather than at signal decay. Investigate whether entry criteria are systematically placing you into event windows
The system is performing to specification. Win rate matches the model
The system has broken and should be suspended pending a full rebuild
Variance. Twenty trades is far too small to say anything

explanation.correct: Win rate is the least informative metric here. The shift in loss magnitude plus a common cause across five of six losses is a structural signal, and gap losses point to an entry-side problem worth checking immediately.

distractors.B: Monitoring only the metric that looks fine is how degradation goes unnoticed.
distractors.C: Over-reaction. There is a specific hypothesis to test before a rebuild.
distractors.D: Correct about sample size for the win rate, and it earns half credit for that, but the clustered common cause is exactly the kind of evidence that does not require a large sample.

questions.learning_objective: Monitor loss distribution and failure mode clustering, not just hit rate.

visual.title: Same win rate, worse losses
visual.caption: 70% rate held, but 5 of 6 losses were gaps through the short strike

questions.stem: Which journal field does the most to improve future decisions?

choices.text: The reason you expected the trade to work, written before entry, in falsifiable terms
The profit or loss in pounds
A screenshot of the chart at entry
How you felt during the trade

explanation.correct: A pre-registered falsifiable thesis is the only field that lets you later separate a good decision from a good outcome. Everything else is recorded after you know the answer.

distractors.B: P and L is the outcome, and outcome tells you nothing about decision quality on any single trade.
distractors.C: Useful context, and it earns partial credit, but a chart can be read to support any story once the result is known.
distractors.D: Emotional state is genuinely valuable for pattern-finding, which is why it scores half, but on its own it does not test the decision.

questions.learning_objective: Pre-register a falsifiable thesis so decision quality can be assessed independently of outcome.

scenario.text: You have identified a candidate credit spread on QQQ. Rank the following in execution order. Position 1 is first.

questions.stem: Rank the steps.

choices.text: Confirm no macro print or earnings inside the expiry window
Confirm current portfolio beta-weighted delta leaves room for this position
Select strikes from the delta target
Calculate contract count from max loss and risk budget
Set the profit target, the stop and the time stop
Submit the order at the mid and work it

explanation.correct: Portfolio-level room must be confirmed before sizing, because a position that fits the per-trade budget can still break the portfolio. Exits must be defined before the order goes live, or they are not exits, they are reactions.

distractors.note: Placing E after F is scored as a hard failure regardless of the rest of the ordering. Deciding exits while carrying live risk is the behaviour the constraint is designed to catch.

questions.learning_objective: Sequence portfolio checks and exit definition before order submission.

questions.stem: Select every reason a No Trade decision should be logged with the same rigour as an executed trade.

choices.text: It measures whether gates are actually being applied or quietly skipped
It builds the counterfactual dataset needed to test whether any gate is too strict
It reveals whether rejections cluster in particular regimes, symbols or times of day
It creates a record for tax purposes
It provides a behavioural check on whether rejection rate collapses during drawdowns

explanation.correct: A, B, C and E. The last is the most valuable and the least obvious: a rejection rate that falls when you are losing is a measurable early-warning signal of discipline breakdown, visible before the P and L shows it.

distractors.D: No transaction occurred, so there is nothing to report.

questions.learning_objective: Instrument the No Trade path as a first-class dataset.

scenario.text: Account value 50,000. Risk per trade is capped at 2 percent. The candidate spread is 5 wide, sold for 1.40, so max loss is 360 per contract.

questions.stem: How many contracts?

choices.text: 2 contracts, because 2.78 must round down
3 contracts, because 2.78 rounds to 3 and the overage is trivial
2.78 contracts is not tradeable, so widen the spread until the number is whole
7 contracts, since the 1,000 risk budget divided by the 140 credit gives 7

explanation.correct: 1,000 divided by 360 is 2.78, and sizing rules always round down. Rounding up means the limit is not a limit.

distractors.B: 3 contracts is 1,080, which is 2.16 percent. Small in isolation, and it establishes that the cap can be exceeded when convenient.
distractors.C: Widening the spread to make the arithmetic tidy raises risk per contract to serve a cosmetic goal.
distractors.D: Sizing on credit received rather than on capital at risk. This produces roughly 2.5x the intended exposure and is the most dangerous error on the list.

questions.learning_objective: Size from capital at risk and always round down.

scenario.text: A strategy wins 70 percent of the time for 140 and loses 30 percent of the time for 360, held to expiry with no management.

questions.stem: What is the expected value per trade, and what follows?

choices.text: Minus 10. A 70 percent win rate is not sufficient, and the strategy is only viable if active management shifts the loss side
Plus 98. The win side dominates
Plus 42. Net of the loss contribution the strategy is profitable
Zero. Defined-risk strategies are break-even before costs by construction

explanation.correct: 0.70 times 140 is 98, 0.30 times minus 360 is minus 108, giving minus 10 before commissions. High win rate with an unmanaged tail is a losing structure, which is exactly why managed exits at 50 percent and 21 DTE exist.

distractors.B: Counts only the favourable branch.
distractors.C: Arithmetic error, and the direction of the error is the seductive one.
distractors.D: No such construction exists.

questions.learning_objective: Compute expectancy and understand why win rate alone is meaningless.

visual.title: Expected value per trade
visual.caption: EV = 98 − 108 = −10 per trade — a losing strategy held to expiry

scenario.text: Your open book: short put spreads on NVDA, AMD, MSFT, QQQ and SMH. Each is 1.5 percent of the account, so 7.5 percent total. Each individually passes the risk budget.

questions.stem: Select every statement that is true.

choices.text: In a broad technology selloff these five behave much closer to one position than five, so effective concentration is far above 1.5 percent
QQQ and SMH overlap materially with the three single names, so the book is doubly concentrated
Beta-weighted portfolio delta is the correct measure of the aggregate exposure, not the sum of individual max losses
Because every position is defined risk, the true worst case remains bounded at 7.5 percent
Correlation among these names tends to rise precisely in the selloffs that would hurt this book

explanation.correct: A, B, C and E. The bound in D is arithmetically true and is the wrong mental model: 7.5 percent taken all at once, in a single correlated event, is a different risk from 7.5 percent spread across independent outcomes, and correlation rises exactly when you need it not to.

distractors.D: True as a number, misleading as a risk assessment. This is the answer that separates traders who compute risk from traders who understand it.

questions.learning_objective: Measure correlated concentration rather than summing independent max losses.

visual.title: Five names, one bet
visual.caption: Each passes the 1.5% budget; correlated, they act like one 7.5% trade

scenario.text: Net liquidation 120,000. Buying power used 74,000. Beta-weighted portfolio delta against SPY is minus 340. Aggregate short vega is minus 900. VIX is 15.8 and IV rank across the book averages 22.

questions.stem: SPY falls 5 percent overnight and VIX doubles. Which observation should drive tonight's action?

choices.text: Short vega of minus 900 into an IV rank of 22 is the binding problem. A vol doubling from a low base produces a mark-to-market loss and a buying power expansion that could force liquidation at the worst prices
Minus 340 beta-weighted delta is the binding problem, implying roughly 3,400 dollars of directional loss per 1 percent SPY move
Buying power usage at 62 percent is the binding problem and should be cut to 50 percent
Nothing needs to change. Every position is individually defined risk

explanation.correct: Delta loss is roughly 17,000 on a 5 percent move and is real but calculable. The vega and margin interaction is what turns a survivable loss into a forced one, because buying power requirements expand as volatility rises, exactly when the mark is worst.

distractors.B: Correct arithmetic and a genuine concern, scoring well, but it treats the position as static. Delta will steepen as the short strikes are approached.
distractors.C: A reasonable policy target, but stated without reference to what the scenario actually does to the requirement.
distractors.D: Individually defined risk with correlated positions and a margin system that expands under stress is precisely how defined-risk books get liquidated.

questions.learning_objective: Model buying power expansion under vol shock, not just mark-to-market loss.

visual.title: Book greeks vs the shock
visual.caption: SPY −5% & VIX doubles → short delta AND short vega both hurt at once

questions.stem: For an account under 50,000 dollars, what is the strongest argument for defined-risk structures over undefined-risk ones, even when the undefined version has better expectancy?

choices.text: A single tail event cannot end the account, which preserves the ability to keep trading the edge for long enough that expectancy can express itself
Defined-risk structures have higher win rates
Defined-risk structures are cheaper in commissions
Brokers do not permit undefined risk on small accounts

explanation.correct: Expectancy is a property of a long run, and you only reach the long run if you survive every short run. Capping the tail buys survival.

distractors.B: Usually the reverse. Buying the wing lowers the win rate.
distractors.C: Defined risk normally costs more in commissions, not less.
distractors.D: Often true as a permissioning matter, and it earns some credit, but it is a constraint rather than a reason.

questions.learning_objective: Understand risk of ruin as the constraint that makes expectancy accessible.

scenario.text: Your edge estimate implies a full Kelly fraction of about 9 percent of capital per trade. Your current fixed-fractional rule risks 1.5 percent.

questions.stem: What is the best assessment?

choices.text: Stay well below Kelly. The fraction is extremely sensitive to estimation error in the edge, and overestimating edge by a modest amount pushes you past the growth-optimal point into a region with severe drawdowns
Move to half Kelly at 4.5 percent, which is the standard compromise
Move to full Kelly. It is by definition growth-optimal
Kelly does not apply to options, so ignore it

explanation.correct: Kelly assumes the edge is known. In trading it is estimated from a small sample, and the penalty curve is asymmetric: being over is much worse than being under. A 9 percent implied fraction is itself evidence the edge estimate is inflated.

distractors.B: Half Kelly is a real and defensible convention, scoring well, but applying it to a suspect edge estimate inherits the estimation error and triples your current risk.
distractors.C: Growth-optimal only under a known distribution that you do not have.
distractors.D: The framework applies wherever there is a repeated bet with an edge.

questions.learning_objective: Treat Kelly as an upper bound on a noisy estimate rather than a target.

visual.title: Kelly vs your rule
visual.caption: Full Kelly is a ceiling, not a target — fractional Kelly survives a bad edge estimate

questions.stem: You are down 40 percent from the account high. What gain on the remaining capital returns you to the high, and what does that imply for sizing during drawdown?

choices.text: 66.7 percent, which is why risk per trade should generally be reduced in drawdown rather than increased, since the recovery burden grows faster than the loss
40 percent, which means recovery is symmetric with the loss
66.7 percent, which is why risk per trade should be increased to recover faster
About 50 percent, and sizing should be held constant throughout

explanation.correct: 1 divided by 0.6 is 1.667, so 66.7 percent. The convexity of the recovery requirement is the entire argument for defending capital early rather than trading harder late.

distractors.B: The most common intuitive error, and it understates the problem badly.
distractors.C: Correct arithmetic attached to the conclusion that destroys accounts. Getting the number right and the response wrong is worse than getting both wrong.
distractors.D: Wrong number, and constant sizing through a deep drawdown ignores what the convexity implies.

questions.learning_objective: Internalise drawdown convexity and its implication for sizing.

visual.title: Drawdown is not symmetric
visual.caption: Down 40% needs +66.7% on what is left just to get back to even

scenario.text: Core CPI comes in at 0.4 percent month on month against 0.2 percent expected. Rate futures immediately reprice to remove one cut from the next twelve months. SPY is down 1.3 percent, the 2 year yield is up 14 basis points, and VIX is up 3.2 points.

questions.stem: You hold short-dated short put spreads on SPY. What is the most useful immediate read?

choices.text: The move is a repricing of the rate path rather than a growth shock, so the vol expansion is more likely to decay over days than to compound, but that is a probabilistic lean and not a reason to override your exit rules
Vol has expanded, so add to the short put spreads at better prices
A hot inflation print reliably marks the start of a sustained downtrend, so close everything
CPI affects bonds, not equity index options, so nothing has changed for your positions

explanation.correct: A front-end-led move with the 2 year leading is a policy repricing. These typically produce a vol spike that fades, but the honest version of that view includes its own uncertainty and does not license overriding rules.

distractors.B: Adding to a losing position during an active repricing is the correct instinct about vol attached to the wrong moment.
distractors.C: Single prints have poor predictive power for sustained trends.
distractors.D: The rate path is a primary driver of equity index vol.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish a policy repricing from a growth shock and calibrate confidence accordingly.

visual.title: Hot CPI print
visual.caption: Rates repriced to remove a cut — a rates shock, not an equity-specific one

scenario.text: FOMC decision is tomorrow at 14:00 ET. SPY options expiring the day after show ATM IV of 22 percent. Options expiring 30 days out show 15 percent. A cut is 92 percent priced. The statement and the projections are released together.

questions.stem: Which is the most accurate characterisation of the opportunity?

choices.text: The front expiry carries an event premium that will collapse within minutes of 14:00 regardless of direction, but with a cut 92 percent priced the market risk sits in the projections and the press conference, not the decision itself
With a cut 92 percent priced, the outcome is effectively known, so selling front-expiry premium is close to a free roll
22 percent front IV against 15 percent at 30 days is a mispricing to be arbitraged with a calendar
FOMC days are unpredictable, so no position should be held into them

explanation.correct: Priced decisions are rarely where the volatility comes from. The projections and the tone of the press conference carry the surprise, and the crush happens whichever way price moves.

distractors.B: The decision being priced is precisely why the reaction is driven by everything else. Treating a priced outcome as a free roll is how event sellers get hurt.
distractors.C: The front-back gap is event premium, not a mispricing. A calendar is a legitimate way to express the view and earns real credit, but calling the gap an arbitrage misunderstands what it is.
distractors.D: Avoidance is a valid personal policy and it does no harm, but it is not an analysis.

questions.learning_objective: Locate where event risk actually sits when the headline outcome is already priced.

visual.title: SPY IV into the FOMC
visual.caption: A cut is 92% priced — the front premium is event vol that will crush after

scenario.text: Over three weeks: utilities and staples outperform, technology and discretionary lag, the 10 year yield falls 28 basis points, high yield credit spreads widen 34 basis points, and the index itself is down only 1.1 percent.

questions.stem: What is the most defensible interpretation?

choices.text: Defensive rotation with credit confirming, which argues for reducing net short-put delta and lowering the delta of new short strikes, even though the index has barely moved
Ordinary rotation noise, since the index is down only 1.1 percent
Falling yields are bullish for equities, so this is a buying opportunity in technology
Widening credit spreads always precede a recession, so move to cash

explanation.correct: Credit widening alongside a defensive equity rotation and a bid for duration is a coherent risk-off signature. The flat index is the point: internals move before the headline does.

distractors.B: The index level is the least informative variable in the set.
distractors.C: Yields falling because growth expectations are falling is not the same as yields falling because inflation is easing. The credit spread widening tells you which one this is.
distractors.D: Directionally aware but over-committed. Spread widening of this size is common and mostly does not precede recession.

questions.learning_objective: Read internals and credit as leading signals rather than watching the index level.

visual.title: Three weeks of rotation
visual.caption: Defensive leadership + wider credit = risk-off under a flat index

scenario.text: Non-farm payrolls print at 310,000 against 175,000 expected. Average hourly earnings are in line. The unemployment rate ticks up to 4.2 percent from 4.1 percent because the participation rate rose. Equities rally, the 10 year yield rises 6 basis points.

questions.stem: Why did equities rally despite a hot headline number?

choices.text: The composition was benign. Wages in line and a participation-driven rise in unemployment point to expanding labour supply rather than an overheating wage spiral, so the growth is not inflationary
Strong payrolls are always bullish for equities
The unemployment rate rising is the dominant signal and implies imminent cuts
The 6 basis point yield move shows the bond market disagreed, and equities are simply wrong

explanation.correct: Composition beats headline. Supply-driven employment growth without wage acceleration is the combination markets welcome, because it delivers growth without forcing the policy path higher.

distractors.B: Hot payrolls with hot wages usually sell off. The sign is regime-dependent.
distractors.C: Partly reasonable and worth credit, but a participation-driven uptick is not labour market weakness.
distractors.D: A 6 basis point move is a modest repricing consistent with the equity reaction, not a disagreement.

questions.learning_objective: Read the composition of a data release rather than the headline print.

visual.title: Hot payrolls, market rallies
visual.caption: A rising participation rate reads as healthy supply, not overheating

scenario.text: VIX jumps from 14 to 27 in two sessions. However, the VIX futures curve stays in mild contango beyond the front month, VVIX rises only modestly from 92 to 104, SKEW is roughly unchanged, and the move is concentrated in a single sector on an identifiable regulatory headline.

questions.stem: What does the divergence most likely indicate, and what follows for a premium seller?

choices.text: The options market is pricing a localised shock rather than systemic stress. Selling elevated vol has better than usual odds, but the divergence is an inference from second-order signals rather than a guarantee, so it justifies a normal-sized defined-risk position, not a larger one
VIX at 27 is a systemic warning regardless of the other signals, so reduce exposure
The divergence confirms the spike is false, which justifies sizing up to take advantage of a rare clean signal
VVIX and SKEW are secondary indicators with no practical predictive value

explanation.correct: A spike without a curve inversion, without a vol-of-vol expansion and without tail repricing looks like an idiosyncratic event. The discipline being tested is separating a better-than-usual read from a licence to increase size.

distractors.B: Reacting to the headline number while ignoring the confirming indicators, which is over-caution rather than analysis.
distractors.C: Correct analysis, wrong conclusion. Confidence in a read is not the same as reduced risk, and sizing up on a confident read is a recurring path to large losses.
distractors.D: Both carry information about how the market is pricing tail and vol-of-vol risk.

questions.learning_objective: Read vol complex divergence, and keep analytical confidence separate from position size.

visual.title: VIX spike — but the internals?
visual.caption: Contango + calm VVIX/SKEW + single sector = a localised shock, not systemic

questions.stem: Select every statement that is generally true about implied volatility around a single-name earnings event.

choices.text: Front-cycle IV typically rises into the event and drops sharply immediately after the release
The term structure typically inverts, with the expiry containing the event carrying higher IV than later expiries
The implied move derived from the ATM straddle is on average close to, and frequently above, the subsequent realised move
The crush occurs only if the stock fails to move materially
Elevated pre-earnings IV mainly reflects a directional view held by the market

explanation.correct: A, B and C. Event premium builds into the release, inverts the near-term curve, and on average sits at or slightly above realised, which is the structural basis for earnings premium selling.

distractors.D: The crush happens because the uncertainty resolves, not because the move was small. A stock can gap 8 percent and the IV still collapses.
distractors.E: IV is a magnitude expectation and is direction-agnostic. Skew, not IV level, carries directional information.

questions.learning_objective: Understand the mechanics of the earnings vol cycle, especially that crush is independent of direction.
